blocks.title: You'll want to know: lectulus, lectulī

segments.text: lectulus, lectulī — "a little bed, a small couch".
In cubiculō parvō lectulus dūrus est. In the small bedroom there is a hard little bed.
Second declension, masculine: lectulus, lectulī m., a diminutive of lectus 'bed'.
lectulus is a diminutive of lectus 'bed, couch' (Lewis & Short), which is usually traced to PIE legʰ- 'to lie down'.
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.

lessons.title: strāmentum, strāmentī — straw bedding, straw; a covering

segments.text: Before the new one: say the Latin for hospitable, then the Latin for a little bed.

blocks.title: You'll want to know: strāmentum, strāmentī

segments.text: strāmentum, strāmentī — "straw bedding, straw; a covering".
Pauper in strāmentō dormit, nōn in lectō. The poor man sleeps on straw, not in a bed.
Second declension, neuter: strāmentum, strāmentī n. Straw spread out for sleeping on, or for animals.
strāmentum is built on sternō 'to spread' (Lewis & Short), from its participle strātus, with the suffix -mentum: something spread out to lie on.
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.

blocks.title: You'll want to know: teges, tegetis

segments.text: teges, tegetis — "a mat, a rush mat; a covering".
In caupōnā parvā tantum teges in pavīmentō est. In a small inn there is only a mat on the floor.
Third declension, feminine: teges, tegetis f. A coarse mat of rushes, the poor man's bed in Roman satire.
teges is built on tegō 'to cover' (Lewis & Short): a covering, a mat.
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.

lessons.title: cervīcal, cervīcālis — a pillow, a bolster

blocks.title: You'll want to know: cervīcal, cervīcālis

segments.text: cervīcal, cervīcālis — "a pillow, a bolster".
Hospes cervīcal sub caput pōnit et dormit. The guest puts a pillow under his head and sleeps.
Third declension, neuter: cervīcal, cervīcālis n. Literally a thing for the neck.
cervīcal is built on cervīx, cervīcis 'neck' (EtymDB; Lewis & Short): a support for the neck. English cervical comes from cervīx.

lessons.title: lōdīx, lōdīcis — a blanket, a coverlet

segments.text: Before the new one: say the Latin for a mat, then the Latin for a pillow.

blocks.title: You'll want to know: lōdīx, lōdīcis

segments.text: lōdīx, lōdīcis — "a blanket, a coverlet".
Nox frīgida est, sed lōdīx tenuis est. The night is cold, but the blanket is thin.
Third declension, feminine: lōdīx, lōdīcis f. A wool blanket for a bed.
The origin of lōdīx is not settled: Lewis & Short give the sense, a blanket or coverlet, but no source, and EtymDB does not list it.
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.

segments.text: To put in? (appellō, appellere.) To step out? (ēgredior, ēgredī.) To haul ashore? (subdūcō, subdūcere.) To launch? (dēdūcō, dēdūcere.) Navigable? (nāvigābilis, nāvigābile.) To toss on the waves? (flūctuō, flūctuāre.) To be seasick? (nauseō, nauseāre.) To carry down? (dēferō, dēferre.) To take across? (trāiciō, trāicere.) To swim to safety? (ēnatō, ēnatāre.) A harbour? (portus, portūs.) A dockyard? (nāvāle, nāvālis.) A tidal inlet? (aestuārium, aestuāriī.) A lighthouse? (pharus, pharī.) A headland? (prōmunturium, prōmunturiī.) The open sea? (salum, salī.) The high sea? (pelagus, pelagī.) The level sea? (aequor, aequoris.) Of the sea? (marīnus, marīna, marīnum.) Coastal? (maritimus, maritima, maritimum.) A sandbank? (syrtis, syrtis.) A billow? (flūctus, flūctūs.) A shallow? (vadum, vadī.) A strait? (fretum, fretī.) To sail past? (praetervehor, praetervehī.) A dead calm? (malacia, malaciae.) Calm weather? (tranquillitās, tranquillitātis.) A peninsula? (paenīnsula, paenīnsulae.) Of the shore? (lītoreus, lītorea, lītoreum.) To sail out? (ēnāvigō, ēnāvigāre.) A roadside inn? (dēverticulum, dēverticulī.) To lodge? (dēversor, dēversārī.) To spend the night? (pernoctō, pernoctāre.) A stable-keeper? (stabulārius, stabulāriī.) Hospitable? (hospitālis, hospitāle.) A little bed? (lectulus, lectulī.) Straw bedding? (strāmentum, strāmentī.) A mat? (teges, tegetis.) A pillow? (cervīcal, cervīcālis.) A blanket? (lōdīx, lōdīcis.)
